plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs covered in rose-like blooms with layered petals and golden centers. Flowers stand out against dark leaves on cold winter days, so they brighten gardens when little else is in flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring, peaking in midwinter
plants.location: Japan, the southeastern United States, and mild-winter gardens in western Europe
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative of the Japanese camellia, gives us tea. Japanese camellias are grown for their flowers, and their seeds are pressed into camellia oil.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima
plants.description: A dramatic Australian wildflower with a crimson flower head the size of a fist. The head is a dome of tightly packed florets, ringed by petal-like bracts. It stands out in the bushland of the southern hemisphere summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly spring, from September to November, with occasional late blooms into early summer
plants.location: Sandstone bushland around Sydney, New South Wales, Australia
plants.funFact: The waratah is the floral emblem of New South Wales. Its flower head is a cluster of many small flowers, and honeyeater birds pollinate it.
